root_cause_classification.reason: The measured regression appears in prefill and dense forward timing while logits and sampling timing are nearly unchanged. The opt-in sidecar kernel performs scalar host matvec work and decodes the fp16 Q8_0 scale from packed bytes inside the innermost per-weight loop, causing each 32-value Q8 block scale to be decoded repeatedly instead of once per block. Eager F32 Candle remains faster on the bounded i5-8250U artifact despite the larger F32 materialization.

Keep packed sidecar execution opt-in and exact-tensor scoped.

Avoid per-weight block-offset arithmetic in the innermost loop.
Use bounded scratch only if it is reused across calls or explicitly measured.

Compare against the existing eager F32 behavior oracle with identical prompt IDs, generated IDs, decoded text, selected backend/kernel identity, dense hook-selection identity, and fallback_used=false.
Do not claim speedup unless a separate bounded timing artifact proves it.
